newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late palm olein stable, trade quiet.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late palm olein stable, trade quiet.

text.p: Limited buying interest amid ample supply kept Indonesian palm olein prices generally soft in late trading on Friday, traders said.
They said olein stayed at 1,345-50 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, but quotes were also heard at 1,340. Crude palm oil was holding at around 1,145 rupiah/kg in Medan.

The traders said news that production from state plantations were expected to fall by about 20 percent this year did not have any immediate impact on the market as most players had wound down their business for the day ahead of the weekend.
An agriculture ministry official told Reuters that state plantations were experiencing a drop in output because of the weather, ageing trees and last year's fertiliser shortage.
The official also said that state-run marketing agency KPB had resumed signing crude palm oil export contracts for November after a freeze in October due to overselling.
He said KPB had committed itself to about 100,000 tonnes in September, which was about twice its monthly exports.
"I think local prices will begin to firm up next week because of the news," one trader said. "It was a little late in the day for the market to react."
